questions.question:
**Direction: Identity the appropriate choice in changing the voice of the following sentence.**

She was knitting a sweater at that time.

options.text: A sweater was being knitted by her at that time.
A sweater was being knitted by her at this time.
She knitted a sweater at that time.
A Sweater has been knitted by her at that time.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'****A sweater was being knitted by her at that time.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in Past Continuous Tense and in Active Voice.
 
• The rule for changing a Past Continuous Tense from Active voice to Passive voice or Passive to Active Voice:
 
• Interchange the object and subject with each other, i.e. object of the active sentence become the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• Structure: 
 
 
• Subject + was/were + v1 + ing + object (Active Voice)__
 
• Object + was/were + being + V3 + by Subject __(Passive Voice)__ 
 
 
 
• Example: 
 __
 
• *Esha was singing a song.** *(Active Voice)
 
• *A song was being sung by Esha. *(Passive Voice)
 
 
 
• ​Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 ​​​

Correct sentence__:* A sweater was being knitted by her at that time.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **__Mistake Points__**

 
• There may be confusion between Options 1 and 2.
 
• **"This"** is changed to **"That"** in the case of narration (Direct to Indirect Speech) and not in the case of voices.

__
 
• The phrase **"the icing on the cake"** means something **that makes a good situation even better. **(केक पर आइसिंग)

 
 
• **Example: **Getting a promotion was great, but getting a bonus was** the icing on the cake.**
 
 
 
• **"The icing on the cake" **refers to an additional benefit or positive aspect that enhances an already good situation. (केक पर आइसिंग)
 
 
• **Example: **Winning the championship was a dream come true for the team, but being awarded the MVP trophy was **the icing on the cake.**
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Example:** Losing the job was tough, but **the silver lining **was that it pushed him to start his own business.

• **Example: **He was tempted by the offer, but he knew it was just a** bird in the bush.**
 
 
 
• **A cold turkey** (ठंडा टर्की): To quit something abruptly, especially an addiction.
 
 
• **Example:** He decided to quit smoking **cold turkey.**

questions.question:
Rewrite the given below sentence with the suitable usage of the Phrasal verb.

There is a twenty-day cooling-off period in which the investor can choose to ______ of the contract.

options.text: There is a twenty-day cooling-off period in which the investor can choose to back up of the contract.
There is a twenty-day cooling-off period in which the investor can choose to back in of the contract.
There is a twenty-day cooling-off period in which the investor can choose to back to the contract.
There is a twenty-day cooling-off period in which the investor can choose to back out of the contract.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c4b11ae370ac051f001bd05f7c84da00a439639bbc7ad21a1eefc4780d8da925.png] Explanation –

__
 
• The blank space is to be filled with phrasal verbs. Let's understand **what are phrasal verbs.**
 
• A **Phrasal verb** is a phrase (such as *take-off* or *look down on*) that combines a verb with a preposition or adverb or both and that functions as a verb whose meaning is different from the combined meanings of the individual words.
 
• Let's see an example of the phrasal verb.

 
• I ***went out ***of the room for a moment. ​ * [IMAGE: https://lh4.googleusercontent.com/YY4YZTH40SO3_UpAJPreYICI3r-4cV_-RhuEiggUtqZ8_9yb_nK6ruGII6ib8QMJeZ9Pxe_ZhoLcYeFJJ07WA8rQpfAdyZ7jkzCdks3XiXWSvx7s1KDiv9hAJP3gtGKw7PqCOao] *

 
• Let's find out the phrasal verb suitable for the given sentence.
 
• **Option 1 **is wrong because "Back up means - to support", which is not related to the sentence.
 
• **Option 2 & option 3 **are also wrong because "back in" and "back to" are not phrasal verbs. It doesn't have meaning.
 
• The Phrasal verb used in **Option 4 is the correct answer** because "Back out means - to choose not to do something agreed".__ It is suitable for the sentence that is related to the contract.

 [IMAGE: https://lh4.googleusercontent.com/DT4JP1Tl1qXBQ7iUk5vowhZKBex5b5ZiEyZ7L_unjV0FQpxfyB4IkOLkxM8Vo8wKdM1QW0sWIPb87JjfwZDyaYMviPe1h_O0wEfc-oeViBdWsG2EjTu6d1EPscHTbI3UjcrXOI8] The complete sentence will be -* **" There is a twenty-day cooling-off period in which the investor can choose to **back out** of the contract."*

questions.question: Select the sentence structure that is grammatically correct.

options.text: Twenty feel tall the fully grown the dragon tree is about and five feet across.
Twenty feet tall and five feet across the fully grown dragon tree is about.
Twenty feet tall and five feet across is about the fully grown dragon tree.
The fully grown dragon tree is about twenty feet tall and five feet across.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **The fully grown dragon tree is about twenty feet tall and five feet across.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The construction of the sentences is incorrect except option 4. Let's explore all the other options: 

 
• Option 1: *Twenty feel tall the fully grown the dragon tree is about and five feet across. *

 
 
• ​The use of **'and' **after **about** makes the sentence grammatically absurd.
 
 
 
• Option 2: *Twenty feet tall and five feet across the fully grown dragon tree is about.*
 
 
• *​*The sentence doesn't make any grammatical sense.
 
 
 
• Option 3: *Twenty feet tall and five feet across is about the fully grown dragon tree.*
 
 
• ​The use of **'about' **is wrong here. It makes the sentence grammatically incorrect.
 
 
 
• Thus, option 4 is the correct sentence in which the subject is **'**The fully grown dragon tree' and the other part of the sentence describes the **subject. **It makes proper grammatical sense.

**Correct sentence:* ****The fully grown dragon tree is about twenty feet tall and five feet across.*

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.**

Father told his children that he didn't wish to see any of them and ordered them to go away and leave him alone for some time.

Father said to his children:

options.text: "I didn't wish to see any of you. Go away and leave him alone for some time."
"He didn't wish to see any of them. They should go away and leave him alone for some time."
"I am not wishing to see any of you. You may go away and leave me alone for some time."
"I don't wish to see any of you. Go away and leave me alone for some time."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is- "I don't wish to see any of you. Go away and leave me alone for some time."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let's look at the steps to change the sentence from indirect to direct speech:

 
 
• When the indirect speech is in the assertive form, we follow the steps given below:
 
• The pronoun 'he' is replaced by 'I' accordingly. In the same way, the following changes will take place:
 
 
• them- you, him- me.
 
 
 
• The auxiliary verb 'didn't' is replaced by 'don't' followed by the 1st form of the verb i.e. wish.
 
• The latter part of the sentence is an imperative sentence, hence its direct form will be as:
 
 
• V1 + Obejct.
 
 
 
• At last line up the remaining part.

 
 
 

Following these steps, we finally get-* Father said to his children, "I don't wish to see any of you. Go away and leave me alone for some time."*

questions.question:
Direction: The following passage consists of six sentences. The first and the sixth sentences are given. The middle four sentences in each have been removed and jumbled up. These are labeled P, Q, R, and S. You are required to find out the proper sequence of the four sentences and choose the correct order from the options.

S1: If you’re a woman in your 20s, you probably think you don’t have to worry about health problems such as strokes and colon cancer yet.

S6: Protect yourself from conditions increasingly affecting younger women.

P: But according to new research, they could affect you sooner than you think. 

Q: Recent studies indicate that some disorders associated with older age are affecting younger adults, while others are greatly influenced by what you do in your 20s and 30s.

R: “But it’s important to know that these risk factors are largely preventable."

S: “With the epidemic of obesity and sedentary lifestyles, we’re seeing a rise in risk factors like high cholesterol, smoking, and high blood pressure in younger adults,” says Erin Michos, M.D., M.H.S.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'PQSR.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• While arranging the parts of the passage given in options, we have to find some grammatical or contextual connections between them__, so let’s find out. 

 __
 
• The first statement in the sequence should be the one that best connects with S1.
 
• It should be a continuation or extension of S1.
 
• P follows S1 because it is talking about the new research which is connected to Q.
 
• Q follows P because it is talking about recent studies that indicate that some disorders are associated with older age.
 
• S follows Q because it is talking about the epidemic of obesity and sedentary lifestyles explained by Erin Michos.
 
• R follows S because it is directly connected to S6.
 
• S6 provides a conclusion to the story.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the sequence is 'S1PQSRS6.'
 
• Thus, the correct answer is 'PQSR.'
 
• ​​The correct sequence__:

S1- If you’re a woman in your 20s, you probably think you don’t have to worry about health problems such as strokes and colon cancer yet.

P- But according to new research, they could affect you sooner than you think. 

Q- Recent studies indicate that some disorders associated with older age are affecting younger adults, while others are greatly influenced by what you do in your 20s and 30s.

S- “With the epidemic of obesity and sedentary lifestyles, we’re seeing a rise in risk factors like high cholesterol, smoking and high blood pressure in younger adults,” says Erin Michos, M.D., M.H.S.

R- “But it’s important to know that these risk factors are largely preventable."

S6- Protect yourself from conditions increasingly affecting younger women.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

__
 
• Steps for solving Para Jumbles:
 
 
• Clues include pronouns, like he, she, it, this, that, these, those; adverbs like formally, really; article a, an and the; definers like actually, finally, another; connectors like but, yet, both, also and neither nor, or, however, nevertheless.
 
• Now, with the help of clues, try to find out qualifier and qualified sentences, so that we can make pairs of qualified and qualifier sentences to eliminate the wrong choices given in the question.
 
• After making pairs, start eliminating the wrong choices or options given in the question.
 
• In case there is more than one choice, try to follow the sequence of sentences according to the occurrence of the events.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__** 

__
 
• विकल्पों में दिए गए गद्यांश के भागों को व्यवस्थित करते समय, हमें उनके बीच कुछ व्याकरणिक या प्रासंगिक संबंध खोजने होंगे, तो आइए जानें।
 
 
• अनुक्रम में पहला कथन वह होना चाहिए जो S1 के साथ सर्वोत्तम रूप से जुड़ता हो।
 
• यह S1 की निरंतरता या विस्तार होना चाहिए।
 
• P, S1 का अनुसरण करता है क्योंकि यह new research के बारे में बात कर रहा है जो Q से जुड़ा है।
 
• **Q, P का अनुसरण करता है** क्योंकि यह recent studies में बात कर रहा है जो दर्शाता है कि older age disorder से जुड़े हैं।
 
• **S, Q का अनुसरण करता है** क्योंकि यह Erin Michos द्वारा समझाया गया मोटापा और गतिहीन जीवन शैली की महामारी के बारे में बात कर रहा है।
 
• R, S का अनुसरण करता है क्योंकि यह सीधे S6 से जुड़ा है।
 
• S6 कहानी को एक निष्कर्ष प्रदान करता है।
 
 
 
• इसलिए, अनुक्रम 'S1PQSRS6' है।

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with suitable alternative to make it a meaningful sentence:

Deva was an amazing dancer. He ______ since his childhood.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**has been performing**'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The verb phrase "**has been performing**" is in the present perfect continuous tense, which is used to describe an action that started in the past and is still ongoing or relevant.
 
• In this sentence, "**since his childhood**" indicates an action that began in the past and continues up to the present, making present perfect continuous tense appropriate.
 
• **Option 2** ("have been performing") is incorrect because "Deva" is a singular subject, requiring "has" instead of "have."
 
• **Option 3** ("had performed") is incorrect because the past perfect tense is used for actions completed before another past action, which is not the case here.
 
• **Option 4** ("has performed") is incorrect because it doesn’t convey the ongoing nature of the action.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to change the sentence from direct speech to indirect speech " I have been walking along the river", he said. He said that he ________ along the river.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Had been walking**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, **"I have been walking along the river", he said**. Backshifting requires changing the present perfect continuous tense ('**have been walking**') to the past perfect continuous tense ('**had been walking**').
 
• Consequently, it should be "**He said that he had been walking along the river**" in indirect speech.
 
• This structure (subject + had + been + verb-ing) allows the listener to understand that the action was still going on at the time the person spoke.

Therefore, the correct answer is- ‘**Option 1**’.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• '**Should be walking**' changes the meaning of the sentence, suggesting an obligation or advice instead of stating what was happening.
 
• '**Has to walk**' also introduces an obligation or necessity, which is not implied in the original sentence.
 
• '**Have to walk**' is grammatically incorrect. This option changes the sentence from a statement of a happening to one of an obligation. Furthermore, when using indirect speech with said, a past tense is typically required, which this option does not fulfill.
